children: Indian government bonds weakened on Wednesday as elevated oil prices and a looming 10-year debt sale kept investors defensive.

The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (069436G=CC) yield ended at 7.0447%, up 3.5 basis points from Tuesday, unwinding most of its decline over the previous two sessions. Bond yields move inversely to prices.
Brent crude futures rose towards $100 a barrel in Asian trade as traders weighed oil supply disruptions against hopes that US-Iran shuttle talks could help end the war.
Three commodity vessels crossed the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, well below the 10-day average of about 15, preliminary shipping data showed.
High crude prices, coupled with a weak monsoon, have sharpened inflation concerns and reinforced expectations that the Reserve Bank of India will raise rates at its October 7 meeting.
"We continue to expect rate hikes by the MPC beginning in October, with a 50–75 bps rate hike by the end of FY2027," said Puneet Pal, fixed income head at PGIM India Mutual Fund.
The RBI's open-market bond sales and weekly auctions have added to supply concerns at a time when traders are expecting a rate hike.
Government officials are likely to meet next Friday to finalise the borrowing calendar for the fiscal second half ending in March, two sources said.
The narrow spread between 10-year and 15-year securities could prompt New Delhi to boost longer-dated supply in H2FY27, traders said.
The overnight indexed swap curve rose on Wednesday, pressured by growing paying bets.
"For India, where real yields are quite high but with the central bank likely on the cusp of a rate hike, we have a preference for flatteners," Nomura said in a note.
The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate rose 4 bps to 6.1%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) rate gained 4.35 bps to 6.2950% and the five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate added 3 bps to 6.55%.
